issues.legal_issue: The property chargeable to estate duty on a beneficiary’s death is determined by the change in beneficial interests, not by a change in legal title to trust property.
material_facts: Under the trust, the deceased was entitled to one-third of the trust income during her lifetime, while other beneficiaries were beneficially entitled to the remaining income from the settlor’s death.
On the deceased’s death, the beneficiaries became legal owners of the trust property, but the deceased had no beneficial interest in the other two-thirds of its income.
The estate-duty authorities disputed whether the entire trust estate or only the deceased’s interest passed on her death.
issues.conclusion: Only the deceased’s beneficial interest in the trust property passed on her death; the later change in legal ownership did not make the entire trust estate property passing on her death.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5(1), 2(15) and 2(16) of the Estate Duty Act, whether property passes is assessed by comparing who was beneficially interested immediately before and after death. “Passing” is not a technical expression and means a change in beneficial enjoyment, not merely a change in title. The Court relied on Scott and Coutts and Co. v. Inland Revenue Commissioners, the discussion in Green’s Death Duties, Re Thomas Townsend, Deceased, and Mahendra Rambhai Patel v. Controller of Estate Duty, Gujarat.

rule.if: estate_duty_on_death_assessment and trust_property_exists and deceased_had_limited_beneficial_interest and other_beneficiaries_were_already_beneficially_interested and legal_title_changed_at_death

predicates.estate_duty_on_death_assessment: An estate-duty assessment is made on the basis of property said to pass on a person’s death.
predicates.trust_property_exists: Property is held under a trust for beneficiaries.
predicates.deceased_had_limited_beneficial_interest: The deceased was beneficially entitled to only a defined part of the trust property or its income.
predicates.other_beneficiaries_were_already_benefic: Other beneficiaries had beneficial interests in the trust property before the deceased died.
predicates.legal_title_changed_at_death: Legal ownership of the trust property changed on the deceased’s death.

issues.definition: If an estate-duty assessment concerns trust property, the deceased had only a limited beneficial interest, other beneficiaries were already beneficially interested, and legal title changed at death, only the deceased’s beneficial interest is treated as passing for duty.

issues.legal_issue: A trustee’s personal office, which imposes duties but gives no beneficial or monetary right, is not property passing on the trustee’s death.
material_facts: The deceased was one of the trustees of the trust.
Her trusteeship ended on her death, and her title as trustee gave her no right to the trust property or its income beyond her separate beneficial entitlement.
The trustee’s position had no monetary value and imposed duties rather than conferring a benefit.
issues.conclusion: The deceased’s trustee role was not property passing on her death and could not be included in the estate-duty assessment as property.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5(1) and 2(15) of the Estate Duty Act concern property and interests in property passing on death. A trustee’s personal right, where it has no monetary value, confers no benefit and imposes only duties, is not property for this purpose. The Court applied the beneficial-interest approach reflected in Scott and Coutts and Co. v. Inland Revenue Commissioners, Re Thomas Townsend, Deceased, and Mahendra Rambhai Patel v. Controller of Estate Duty, Gujarat.

rule.if: estate_duty_on_death_assessment and deceased_was_trustee and trustee_role_ended_at_death and trustee_role_conferred_no_benefit_or_monetary_value

predicates.estate_duty_on_death_assessment: An estate-duty assessment is made on the basis of property said to pass on a person’s death.
predicates.deceased_was_trustee: The deceased held the personal office of trustee of a trust.
predicates.trustee_role_ended_at_death: The deceased’s trusteeship ended when the deceased died.
predicates.trustee_role_conferred_no_benefit_or_mon: The trustee’s position gave the deceased no beneficial or monetary right and imposed duties only.

issues.definition: If an estate-duty assessment concerns a deceased trustee whose personal role ended at death and conferred no benefit or monetary value, that role is not treated as dutiable property.
